pr_title: fix(core): Prevent issues with missing or mismatching encryption key
pr_body:
- [x] If `N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY` does not match `configFile.encryptionKey`, fail to init main
- [x] If `N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing on worker, fail to init worker
- [x] If credential decryption fails when attempting to edit a credential, surface [better error message](https://share.cleanshot.com/4DRcwv68)
- [x] If HTTPRN execution fails due to cred decryption error, [block execution](https://share.cleanshot.com/mH8H3Kcg)
- [x] Tests

Story: https://linear.app/n8n/issue/PAY-1184

Hello, 
I'm loading encryption key only from config file, not from env. And this MR broke it. Because it checks only if environment variable is set, which in my case is empty.

Thanks for the comment @Dasio - we discussed it privately but for completeness' sake, we made this change to assert that users would always provide the encryption key in a reliable way; the `config` file is generated at runtime if not existing, which could lead to issues with workers, so in order to prevent this, we added this check.

Sorry for the trouble, you should change the settings to provide the encryption key via environment variable.

issue_context.title: error:1C800064:Provider routines::bad decrypt after update from 1.15.2
issue_context.body:
I'm using n8n via the official Docker Container but when i try to update from 1.15.2 to any newer version i get the error:

"error:1C800064:Provider routines::bad decrypt" and credentials can not be loaded anymore.

The Encryption Key is set via Environment variable but i also checked the config file and it contains the same Encryption key.

After downgrading it works again. Is there any restriction to the Encryption Key as mine has 20 chars with special characters.
comments:
Hey @TauTauBenn,

Can you share how you are running n8n and which recent version you tried? It could be worth checking that you are using the `/home/node/.n8n` path and not `/root/.n8n` as well.

Hi @Joffcom 

i deployed n8n using Azure App Services. I configured the config folder to be "/home/node/n8n" and mounted this to a file share in Azure where the files are then located. Did not change anything on that after the update and before it is working without any problem. Already tried deleting the files etc.

I tried all versions after 1.15.2 one by one.

Hey @TauTauBenn,

Can you double check that path? It should be `/home/node/.n8n`. Can you also share the config values you have set? In theory even if the path is wrong and it is `n8n` instead of `.n8n` we should still use the env option but some platforms may parse the env options in a different way.

yes i had to change it to "/home/node/n8n" via "N8N_USER_FOLDER" without . because azure is not allowing the dot. but n8n is definitely accessing the right folder and creating .cache and .n8n with config etc. in it if i delete the files. 
![image](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/assets/85042590/00bb9a15-5897-4b58-b519-7a39cca3efb8)


I attached a screenshot of the ENV variables.
![image](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/assets/85042590/5822c4ca-1b14-456a-8b3c-21cc28d85436)

I wasn't expecting the `N8N_USER_FOLDER` setting to be there this is why it is handy to see the config. The settings you have other than the one option look to be fine and don't look that different to what I am using. I am not sure why Azure wouldn't allow that path as it is an option in the container so they shouldn't care 🤔 

Can you share the command that is being used to launch the container? I can then see if I am able to reproduce this. The good news is if this is ok in 1.15.2 and not in 1.16.0 it reduces the searching we need to do to track this down.

Yeah sure of course. Azure creates the run command as follows:

`docker run -d --expose=80 --name xxx -e WEBSITE_USE_DIAGNOSTIC_SERVER=false -e WEBSITE_AUTH_ENABLED=False -e WEBSITES_ENABLE_APP_SERVICE_STORAGE=false -e WEBSITE_SITE_NAME=xxx -e PORT=5678 -e WEBSITE_ROLE_INSTANCE_ID=0 -e WEBSITE_HOSTNAME=xxx -e WEBSITE_INSTANCE_ID=xxx -e HTTP_LOGGING_ENABLED=1 n8nio/n8n:latest`

Yeah somewhere between these versions there must be a change which created this...i thought i wait if it maybe get's fixed in a later version but as it is also not working with the latest version now i have to find another solution...

Hey @TauTauBenn,

Is that the complete command I can't see where it is actually mounting the files or setting the env option for the key unless they were just removed.

One other thing I forgot to ask... What special characters are in your key?

At least this is what Azure shows me in the logs... maybe it removes the ENV variables and mounting points from the log. 

Special Characters are: _ + $ § , ! > ( # &

Can you please check once more that the value for the encryption key in `/home/node/.n8n/config` (and not `/home/node/n8n/config`) is identical to the value passed in via env variables in `1.15.2` as well as in one of the later versions.

My theory is that something somewhere is messing up the encryption key value before it's loaded into memory.

Yes it's definitely the same and even if i delete the config file it just creates a new one with exact the same key. If i start it without the ENV variable and only with the one from the config it is giving me the exact same error.

The culprit is definitely https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/7556 which was released in 1.16.0 . But, I'm still not sure under what circumstances would this happen. 
I'll try to look at the code again. but, if that doesn't help we might need a way to re-encrypt your data, so that we can have a look at your encryption key.
